verses.16:18: And he shall go out to the altar that is before the Lord and make atonement upon it; and he shall take some of the blood of the calf and some of the blood of the goat, and put it on the horns of the altar all around.
verses.16:19: And he shall sprinkle some of the blood upon it with his finger seven times, and cleanse it and sanctify it from the uncleannesses of the children of Israel.
verses.16:20: And he shall finish making atonement for the holy place and the tabernacle of testimony and the altar, and he shall make cleansing for the priests; and he shall bring forward the live goat.
verses.16:21: And Aaron shall lay his hands on the head of the live goat, and confess over it all the iniquities of the children of Israel, and all their wrongdoings, and all their sins, and he shall lay them upon the head of the live goat, and send it away by the hand of a ready man into the wilderness.
verses.16:22: And the goat shall bear upon itself their wrongdoings to an untrodden land, and he shall send the goat away into the wilderness.
verses.16:23: And Aaron shall enter into the tabernacle of testimony, and take off the linen robe which he had put on when he entered into the holy place, and shall leave it there.
verses.16:24: And he shall bathe his body in water in a holy place and put on his own robe, and coming out he shall offer his whole burnt offering and the whole burnt offering of the people, and make atonement for himself and for his house and for the people, as for the priests.
verses.16:25: And the fat of the sin offerings he shall offer up upon the altar.
verses.16:26: And he who sends away the goat that was set apart for release shall wash his garments and bathe his body in water, and afterward he shall enter into the camp.
verses.16:27: And the calf for the sin offering and the goat for the sin offering, whose blood was brought in to make atonement in the holy place, they shall carry outside the camp, and they shall burn them completely with fire, both their skins and their flesh and their dung.
verses.16:28: And he who burns them shall wash his garments and bathe his body in water, and afterward he shall enter into the camp.
verses.16:29: And this shall be a perpetual statute for you: in the seventh month humble your souls, and you shall do no work at all, neither the native-born nor the proselyte who dwells among you.
verses.16:30: For on this day he shall make atonement for you, to cleanse you from all your sins before the Lord; and you shall be cleansed.
verses.16:31: This shall be a Sabbath of Sabbaths of rest to you, and you shall humble your souls—a perpetual statute.
verses.16:32: And the priest whom they anoint and whose hands they consecrate to serve as priest after his father shall make atonement, and shall put on the linen robe, a holy robe.
verses.16:33: And he shall make atonement for the Holy of Holies, and for the tabernacle of testimony and for the altar he shall make atonement, and for the priests and for all the congregation he shall make atonement.
verses.16:34: And this shall be a perpetual statute for you, to make atonement for the children of Israel for all their sins." Once a year it shall be done, as the Lord commanded Moses.
verses.17:1: And the Lord spoke to Moses, saying,
verses.17:2: "Speak to Aaron and to his sons and to all the sons of Israel, and you shall say to them, 'This is the word which the Lord has commanded, saying:
verses.17:3: Any man of the sons of Israel, or of the proselytes, or of those joined among you, who slaughters a calf or a sheep or a goat in the camp, and who slaughters outside the camp,
verses.17:4: and does not bring it to the door of the tabernacle of testimony to offer it as a burnt offering or an offering of deliverance to the Lord, acceptable for a sweet aroma—and whoever slaughters outside and does not bring it to the door of the tabernacle of testimony, so as not to present a gift to the Lord before the tabernacle of the Lord—blood shall be reckoned to that man; he has shed blood, and that soul shall be utterly destroyed from its people,
verses.17:5: so that the sons of Israel may bring up their sacrifices, whatever they themselves would slaughter in the fields, and they shall bring them to the Lord at the doors of the tabernacle of testimony, to the priest, and shall sacrifice them as a sacrifice of deliverance to the Lord.
verses.17:6: And the priest shall pour the blood upon the altar all around before the Lord, beside the doors of the tabernacle of testimony, and shall offer up the fat for a sweet aroma to the Lord.
verses.17:7: And they shall no longer sacrifice their sacrifices to the vain things after which they themselves play the harlot. It shall be an everlasting statute for you throughout your generations.'
verses.17:8: And you shall say to them, 'Any man of the sons of Israel, and from the sons of the proselytes who are joined among you, who offers a burnt offering or a sacrifice,
verses.17:9: and does not bring it to the door of the tabernacle of testimony to offer it to the Lord, that man shall be utterly destroyed from his people.
verses.17:10: And any man of the sons of Israel, or of the proselytes who are joined among you, who eats any blood, I will set My face against the soul that eats the blood, and I will destroy it from its people.
verses.17:11: For the life of all flesh is its blood, and I have given it to you upon the altar to make atonement for your souls; for its blood shall make atonement in place of the soul.
verses.17:12: Therefore I have said to the sons of Israel, "No soul among you shall eat blood, nor shall the proselyte who is joined among you eat blood."
verses.17:13: And any man of the sons of Israel, and of the proselytes who are joined among you, who hunts down game, a wild beast or a bird that is eaten, shall pour out the blood and cover it with earth.
verses.17:14: For the life of all flesh is its blood; and I said to the sons of Israel, "You shall not eat the blood of any flesh, for the life of all flesh is its blood; everyone who eats it shall be utterly destroyed."
verses.17:15: And every soul who eats that which died of itself or that which was torn by wild beasts, whether among the native-born or among the proselytes, shall wash his garments and bathe in water, and shall be unclean until evening; then he shall be clean.
verses.17:16: But if he does not wash his garments and does not bathe his body in water, he shall bear his iniquity.'"
verses.18:1: And the Lord said to Moses, saying,
verses.18:2: "Speak to the sons of Israel, and you shall say to them, 'I am the Lord your God.
verses.18:3: According to the practices of the land of Egypt, in which you dwelt, it shall not be done; and according to the practices of the land of Canaan, into which I am bringing you, you shall not do, nor shall you walk in their statutes.
verses.18:4: You shall do My judgments and keep My ordinances, to walk in them; I am the Lord your God.
verses.18:5: And you shall keep all My ordinances and all My judgments, and shall do them; the man who does them shall live by them. I am the Lord your God.
verses.18:6: No man shall approach any close relative of his flesh to uncover nakedness; I am the Lord.
verses.18:7: The nakedness of your father and the nakedness of your mother you shall not uncover; for she is your mother, and you shall not uncover her nakedness.
verses.18:8: The nakedness of your father's wife you shall not uncover; it is your father's nakedness.
verses.18:9: The nakedness of your sister, whether by your father or by your mother, born within the household or outside, her nakedness you shall not uncover.
verses.18:10: The nakedness of your son's daughter or of your daughter's daughter, their nakedness you shall not uncover, for it is your own nakedness.
verses.18:11: The nakedness of the daughter of your father's wife you shall not uncover; she is your sister by the same father, and you shall not uncover her nakedness.
verses.18:12: The nakedness of your father's sister you shall not uncover; for she is a close relative of your father.
verses.18:13: The nakedness of your mother's sister you shall not uncover; for she is a close relative of your mother.
verses.18:14: The nakedness of your father's brother you shall not uncover, and you shall not go in to his wife; for she is your kinswoman.
verses.18:15: The nakedness of your daughter-in-law you shall not uncover; for she is your son's wife, and you shall not uncover her nakedness.
verses.18:16: The nakedness of your brother's wife you shall not uncover; it is your brother's nakedness.
verses.18:17: The nakedness of a woman and of her daughter you shall not uncover; you shall not take her son's daughter or her daughter's daughter to uncover their nakedness, for they are your close relatives; it is an impiety.
verses.18:18: You shall not take a woman in addition to her sister as a rival, to uncover her nakedness beside her while she is still living.
verses.18:19: And you shall not approach a woman in the separation of her uncleanness to uncover her nakedness.
verses.18:20: And you shall not lie with your neighbor's wife to give your seed, to be defiled with her.
verses.18:21: And you shall not give any of your seed to serve a ruler, and you shall not profane the holy name; I am the Lord.
verses.18:22: And with a male you shall not lie as with a woman; for it is an abomination.
verses.18:23: And you shall not lie with any four-footed beast for the giving of seed, to be defiled with it; nor shall a woman stand before any four-footed beast to be mated with it, for it is a loathsome thing.
verses.18:24: Do not defile yourselves with any of these things; for with all these things the nations have been defiled, which I am driving out before your face.
verses.18:25: And the land was defiled; therefore I have repaid them for unrighteousness on its account, and the land loathed those who dwelt upon it.
verses.18:26: And you shall keep all My statutes and all My ordinances, and you shall not do any of all these abominations—neither the native of the land nor the proselyte who has joined himself among you;
verses.18:27: for all these abominations the men of the land who were before you have done, and the land was defiled;
verses.18:28: and lest the land loathe you when you defile it, in the same way that it loathed the nations that were before you.
verses.18:29: For whoever commits any of all these abominations, the souls that commit them shall be utterly destroyed from their people.
verses.18:30: And you shall keep My ordinances, so that you do not practice any of all the abominable customs which were done before you, and you shall not be defiled by them; for I am the Lord your God.'"
verses.19:1: And the Lord spoke to Moses, saying,
verses.19:2: "Speak to the congregation of the sons of Israel, and you shall say to them: 'You shall be holy, for I am holy, the Lord your God.
verses.19:3: Each one shall fear his father and his mother, and you shall keep My Sabbaths; I am the Lord your God.
verses.19:4: You shall not follow after idols, nor shall you make for yourselves molten gods; I am the Lord your God.
verses.19:5: And if you offer a sacrifice of deliverance to the Lord, you shall sacrifice your tenth.
verses.19:6: On whatever day you sacrifice it, it shall be eaten, and on the next day; and if any remains until the third day, it shall be burned up in fire.
verses.19:7: And if it is indeed eaten on the third day, it is unfit for sacrifice; it shall not be accepted.
verses.19:8: And the one who eats it shall bear sin, because he has profaned the holy things of the Lord; and the souls that eat it shall be utterly destroyed from among their people.
verses.19:9: And when you reap the harvest of your land, you shall not finish reaping your harvest of your field, nor shall you gather what falls from your harvest.
verses.19:10: And you shall not glean your vineyard a second time, nor shall you gather the fallen grapes of your vineyard; you shall leave them for the poor and for the sojourner; I am the Lord your God.
verses.19:11: You shall not steal, you shall not lie, nor shall anyone falsely accuse his neighbor.
verses.19:12: And you shall not swear by My name unjustly, nor shall you profane the name of your God; I am the Lord your God.
verses.19:13: You shall not wrong your neighbor, nor rob him; and the wages of a hired servant shall by no means remain overnight with you until morning.
verses.19:14: You shall not speak evil of the deaf, nor put a stumbling block before the blind; but you shall fear the Lord your God; I am the Lord your God.
verses.19:15: You shall do no injustice in judgment; you shall not show partiality to the poor, nor defer to the person of the mighty; in righteousness you shall judge your neighbor.
verses.19:16: You shall not walk in deceit among your nation; you shall not rise up against the blood of your neighbor; I am the Lord your God.
verses.19:17: You shall not hate your brother in your mind; you shall surely reprove your neighbor, and you shall not incur sin because of him.
verses.19:18: And your hand shall not take vengeance, nor shall you bear a grudge against the sons of your people, but you shall love your neighbor as yourself; I am the Lord.
verses.19:19: You shall keep My law. You shall not breed your livestock with another kind, and you shall not sow your vineyard with mixed seed, nor shall you put upon yourself an adulterated garment woven of two materials.
verses.19:20: And if anyone lies carnally with a woman who is a maidservant reserved for a man, and she has not been redeemed with a ransom, nor has freedom been given to her, there shall be an inquiry concerning them; they shall not die, because she was not set free.
verses.19:21: And he shall bring for his trespass to the Lord, to the door of the tabernacle of testimony, a ram for a trespass offering.
verses.19:22: And the priest shall make atonement for him with the ram of the trespass offering before the Lord for the sin which he has sinned, and the sin which he has sinned shall be forgiven him.
verses.19:23: Now when you enter into the land which the Lord God gives you, and plant every kind of tree for food, then you shall cleanse away its uncleanness; for three years its fruit shall be unpurified to you; it shall not be eaten.
verses.19:24: And in the fourth year all its fruit shall be holy, praiseworthy to the Lord;
verses.19:25: and in the fifth year you shall eat the fruit, its produce being an increase for you; I am the Lord your God.
verses.19:26: Do not eat upon the mountains, and you shall not practice augury nor observe birds for omens.
verses.19:27: You shall not make a rounded haircut from the hair of your head, nor shall you mar the appearance of your beard.
verses.19:28: And you shall not make incisions in your body for a departed soul, nor shall you make tattooed marks upon yourselves; I am the Lord your God.
verses.19:29: You shall not profane your daughter to make her a harlot; and the land shall not play the harlot, lest the land be filled with lawlessness.
verses.19:30: You shall keep My Sabbaths, and you shall revere My holy places; I am the Lord.
verses.19:31: You shall not follow after mediums, nor shall you cling to enchanters, to be defiled by them; I am the Lord your God.
verses.19:32: You shall rise up before the gray-headed, and honor the presence of an elder, and fear your God; I am the Lord your God.
verses.19:33: And if any sojourner comes to you in your land, you shall not oppress him.
verses.19:34: The sojourner who comes to you shall be to you as the native-born among you, and you shall love him as yourself; for you were sojourners in the land of Egypt; I am the Lord your God.
verses.19:35: You shall do no injustice in judgment, in measures, in weights, and in balances.
verses.19:36: You shall have just balances, just weights, and a just chous; I am the Lord your God, who brought you out of the land of Egypt.
verses.19:37: And you shall keep all My law and all My ordinances, and perform them; I am the Lord your God.'"
verses.20:1: And the Lord spoke to Moses, saying, "You shall also speak to the sons of Israel:
verses.20:2: 'If anyone of the sons of Israel, or of the sojourners who have come to be in Israel, gives of his seed to a ruler, he shall surely be put to death; the nation upon the land shall stone him with stones.
verses.20:3: And I will set My face against that man, and will destroy him from among his people, because he gave of his seed to a ruler, in order to defile My holy places and to profane the name of those sanctified to Me.
verses.20:4: And if the native-born of the land completely overlook that man with their eyes when he gives of his seed to a ruler, so as not to kill him,
verses.20:5: then I will set My face against that man and against his kindred, and I will destroy him and all who are of one mind with him, so that he plays the harlot after the rulers, from among their people.
verses.20:6: And the soul that follows after mediums or enchanters, to play the harlot after them, I will set My face against that soul and will destroy it from among its people.
verses.20:7: And you shall be holy, for I am holy, the Lord your God;
verses.20:8: and you shall keep My ordinances and perform them; I am the Lord who sanctifies you.
verses.20:9: Whoever speaks evil of his father or his mother shall surely be put to death; he has spoken evil of his father or his mother; he shall be guilty.
verses.20:10: A man who commits adultery with the wife of a man, or who commits adultery with the wife of his neighbor, both the adulterer and the adulteress shall surely be put to death.
verses.20:11: If anyone lies with his father's wife, he has uncovered his father's nakedness; he shall be put to death; both of them are guilty.
verses.20:12: And if anyone lies with his daughter-in-law, both of them shall surely be put to death; for they have committed impiety; they are guilty.
verses.20:13: And whoever lies with a male as with a woman, both of them have committed an abomination; they shall be put to death; they are guilty.
verses.20:14: Whoever takes a woman and her mother, it is a lawless deed; they shall burn up both him and them in fire, so that there shall be no lawlessness among you.
verses.20:15: And whoever lies carnally with a four-footed animal shall surely be put to death, and you shall kill the four-footed animal.
verses.20:16: And any woman who approaches any beast to be mounted by it, you shall kill the woman and the beast; she shall surely be put to death; they are guilty.
verses.20:17: Whoever takes his sister, his father's daughter or his mother's daughter, and sees her nakedness and she sees his nakedness, it is a reproach; they shall be utterly destroyed before the sons of their kindred; he has uncovered his sister's nakedness; they shall bear sin.
verses.20:18: And a man who lies with a woman in her menstrual separation and uncovers her nakedness has uncovered her fountain, and she has uncovered the flow of her blood; both of them shall be utterly destroyed from among their kindred.
verses.20:19: And you shall not uncover the nakedness of your father's sister or of your mother's sister; for he has uncovered his close kin; they shall bear sin.
verses.20:20: Whoever lies with his kinswoman has uncovered the nakedness of his kinswoman; they shall die childless.
verses.20:21: Whoever takes his brother's wife, it is his uncleanness; he has uncovered his brother's nakedness; they shall die childless.
verses.20:22: And keep all My ordinances and My judgments, and perform them; and the land into which I am bringing you to dwell upon it shall by no means loathe you.
verses.20:23: And you shall not walk in the customs of the nations whom I am casting out from before you; for they committed all these things, and I abhorred them.
verses.20:24: And I said to you, "You, inherit their land, and I will give it to you for a possession, a land flowing with milk and honey." I am the Lord your God, who has separated you from all the nations.
verses.20:25: And you shall distinguish them, between the clean beasts and the unclean beasts, and between the clean birds and the unclean; and you shall not make your souls detestable with the beasts, and with the birds, and with all the creeping things of the earth, which I have set apart for you in uncleanness.
verses.20:26: And you shall be holy to Me, for I am holy, the Lord your God, who has separated you from all the nations to be Mine.
verses.20:27: And a man or a woman, whichever of them becomes a medium or an enchanter, both of them shall surely be put to death; stone them with stones; they are guilty.'"
verses.21:1: And the Lord spoke to Moses, saying, "Speak to the priests, the sons of Aaron, and you shall say to them, 'They shall not be defiled for the dead among their nation,
verses.21:2: except for their nearest relative, for father and mother, and for sons and daughters, for a brother,
verses.21:3: and for a virgin sister who is near to him, who has not been given to a husband; for these he may be defiled.
verses.21:4: He shall not be defiled suddenly among his people, so as to profane himself.
verses.21:5: And you shall not shave a bald spot on your head for the dead, and they shall not shave the appearance of their beard, nor shall they make cuttings in their flesh.
verses.21:6: They shall be holy to their God, and they shall not profane the name of their God; for they offer the sacrifices of the Lord, the gifts of their God, and they shall be holy.
verses.21:7: They shall not take a woman who is a harlot and profaned, nor a woman cast out from her husband; he is holy to the Lord his God,
verses.21:8: and he shall sanctify him; he offers the gifts of the Lord your God. He shall be holy, for I, the Lord who sanctifies them, am holy.
verses.21:9: And if the daughter of a man who is a priest is profaned by playing the harlot, she profanes the name of her father; she shall be burned with fire.
verses.21:10: And the high priest among his brethren, upon whose head the anointing oil has been poured and who has been consecrated to wear the garments, shall not remove the turban from his head nor tear his garments,
verses.21:11: nor shall he go in to any dead person; he shall not be defiled for his father nor for his mother,
verses.21:12: nor shall he go out from the holy place, nor profane the sanctuary of his God; for the holy anointing oil of God is upon him. I am the Lord.
verses.21:13: He shall take a virgin from his own lineage;
verses.21:14: but a widow, or a woman cast out, or one profaned, or a harlot—these he shall not take; rather, he shall take a virgin from his own people as a wife,
verses.21:15: and he shall not profane his offspring among his people; I am the Lord who sanctifies him.'"
verses.21:16: And the Lord spoke to Moses, saying,
verses.21:17: "Speak to Aaron, 'A man from your lineage throughout your generations, whoever has a blemish in him, shall not approach to offer the gifts of his God.
verses.21:18: Every man in whom there is a blemish shall not approach: a man who is lame or blind,
verses.21:19: or mutilated in the nose or cut in the ear, a man who has a broken hand or a broken foot,
verses.21:20: or hunchbacked, or having white spots in the eye, or blear-eyed, or a man in whom there is a malignant itch, or a scaly eruption, or having only one testicle—
verses.21:21: everyone in whom there is a blemish from the offspring of Aaron the priest shall not draw near to offer the sacrifices to your God; because there is a blemish in him, he shall not approach to offer the gifts of God.
verses.21:22: The gifts of God, the most holy things and from the holy things, he may eat;
verses.21:23: only he shall not approach the veil, nor draw near to the altar, because he has a blemish; and he shall not profane the sanctuary of his God, for I am the Lord who sanctifies them.'"
verses.21:24: And Moses spoke to Aaron and his sons, and to all the sons of Israel.
verses.22:1: And the Lord spoke to Moses, saying,
verses.22:2: "Speak to Aaron and his sons, and let them take heed regarding the holy things of the sons of Israel, and they shall not profane My holy name in whatever things they sanctify to Me; I am the Lord.
verses.22:3: Say to them, 'Throughout your generations, every man from your offspring who approaches the holy things which the sons of Israel sanctify to the Lord, while his uncleanness is upon him, that soul shall be utterly destroyed from Me; I am the Lord your God.
verses.22:4: And any man from the offspring of Aaron the priest who has leprosy or a discharge shall not eat of the holy things until he is cleansed. And whoever touches any uncleanness of a dead person, or a man from whom an emission of seed goes out,
verses.22:5: whoever touches any unclean creeping thing that defiles him, or a man by whom he is defiled according to all his uncleanness,
verses.22:6: the soul who touches them shall be unclean until evening; he shall not eat from the holy things unless he washes his body with water
verses.22:7: and the sun sets, and he shall be clean; and then he may eat of the holy things, because it is his bread.
verses.22:8: That which dies of itself and that which is torn by wild beasts he shall not eat, so as to be defiled by them; I am the Lord.
verses.22:9: And they shall keep My ordinances, lest they incur sin because of them and die because of it; and if they profane them, I am the Lord God who sanctifies them.
verses.22:10: And no outsider shall eat holy things; a sojourner with a priest or a hired servant shall not eat holy things.
verses.22:11: But if a priest acquires a person purchased with silver, that one may eat of his bread; and those born in his house, they also may eat of his bread.
verses.22:12: And if the daughter of a man who is a priest is married to an outsider, she shall not eat of the firstfruits of the sanctuary.
verses.22:13: And if a priest's daughter becomes a widow, one cast out, and has no offspring, she shall return to her father's house as in her youth; she may eat from her father's bread, and no outsider shall eat from them.
verses.22:14: And a man who eats holy things in ignorance shall add one-fifth of it to it and give the holy thing to the priest.
verses.22:15: And they shall not profane the holy things of the sons of Israel, which they set apart to the Lord,
verses.22:16: and bring upon themselves the iniquity of trespass when they eat their holy things; for I am the Lord who sanctifies them.'"
verses.22:17: And the Lord spoke to Moses, saying,
verses.22:18: "Speak to Aaron and his sons, and to all the congregation of Israel, and you shall say to them, 'Any man from the sons of Israel, or from the sons of the proselytes who are joined to them in Israel, who offers his gifts according to all their pledges or according to all their freewill offerings, whatever they offer to God for a whole burnt offering,
verses.22:19: acceptable for you, shall be unblemished males from the herds and from the sheep and from the goats.
verses.22:20: Whatever has a blemish in it they shall not bring to the Lord, because it shall not be acceptable for you.
verses.22:21: And a man who offers a sacrifice of deliverance to the Lord, having specified a vow according to freewill choice or in your feasts, from the herds or from the sheep, it shall be unblemished to be acceptable; there shall be no blemish in it.
verses.22:22: What is blind, or broken, or cut in the tongue, or having warts, or having a malignant itch, or having scaly eruptions—they shall not bring these to the Lord, and you shall not give any of them as a burnt offering upon the altar to the Lord.
verses.22:23: And a calf or a sheep that is cut in the ear or docked in the tail, you may make them as slaughter-offerings for yourself, but for your vow it shall not be accepted.
verses.22:24: What is crushed, or bruised, or castrated, or torn off—you shall not bring them to the Lord, nor shall you do so in your land.
verses.22:25: And from the hand of a foreigner you shall not offer the gifts of your God from any of these, because there is corruption in them, a blemish is in them; they shall not be accepted for you.'"
verses.22:26: And the Lord spoke to Moses, saying,
verses.22:27: "A calf or a sheep or a goat, when it is born, shall remain seven days under its mother; and on the eighth day and beyond it shall be accepted for gifts, a burnt offering to the Lord.
verses.22:28: And a heifer or a sheep, her and her young ones, you shall not slay in one day.
verses.22:29: And if you sacrifice a sacrifice, a vow of gladness to the Lord, you shall sacrifice it so as to be acceptable for you;
verses.22:30: on that very day it shall be eaten; you shall not leave any of the meat until the morning. I am the Lord.
verses.22:31: And you shall keep My commandments and do them.
verses.22:32: And you shall not profane the name of the Holy One, and I shall be sanctified in the midst of the sons of Israel; I am the Lord who sanctifies you,
verses.22:33: who brought you out of the land of Egypt so as to be your God; I am the Lord."
verses.23:1: And the Lord said to Moses, saying,
verses.23:2: "Speak to the sons of Israel, and you shall say to them: 'The feasts of the Lord, which you shall proclaim as holy convocations, these are My feasts.
verses.23:3: Six days you shall do work, and on the seventh day is a Sabbath of rest, a holy convocation to the Lord; you shall do no work; it is a Sabbath to your Lord in every dwelling of yours.
verses.23:4: These are the feasts to the Lord, and these, proclaim them holy in their appointed seasons.
verses.23:5: In the first month, on the fourteenth day of the month, between the evenings, is the Passover to the Lord.
verses.23:6: And on the fifteenth day of this month is the Feast of Unleavened Bread to the Lord; seven days you shall eat unleavened bread.
verses.23:7: And the first day shall be a holy convocation to you; you shall do no servile work;
verses.23:8: and you shall bring burnt offerings to the Lord for seven days, and the seventh day shall be a holy convocation to you; you shall do no servile work.'"
verses.23:9: And the Lord spoke to Moses, saying,
verses.23:10: "Tell the sons of Israel, and you shall say to them: 'When you enter the land which I give to you and reap its harvest, then you shall bring a sheaf, the firstfruits of your harvest, to the priest;
verses.23:11: and he shall offer up the sheaf before the Lord to be accepted for you; on the day after the first day the priest shall offer it up.
verses.23:12: And you shall prepare on the day on which you bring the sheaf an unblemished year-old sheep for a burnt offering to the Lord,
verses.23:13: and its offering shall be two tenths of fine flour mixed with oil—an offering to the Lord, a sweet-smelling aroma to the Lord—and its drink offering shall be a fourth of a hin of wine.
verses.23:14: And you shall eat neither bread nor roasted new grain until this very day, until you yourselves have brought the gifts to your God; it is an everlasting statute throughout your generations in every dwelling of yours.
verses.23:15: And you shall count for yourselves from the day after the Sabbath, from the day on which you bring the sheaf of the presentation offering, seven complete weeks;
verses.23:16: until the day after the last week you shall count fifty days, and you shall offer a new offering to the Lord.
verses.23:17: From your dwelling you shall bring loaves as a presentation offering, two loaves; they shall be of two tenths of fine flour, and they shall be baked with leaven, as firstfruits to the Lord.
verses.23:18: And he shall bring with the loaves seven unblemished year-old lambs, and one calf from the herd, and two unblemished rams; they shall be a burnt offering to the Lord, together with their offerings and their drink offerings, an offering of sweet-smelling aroma to the Lord.
verses.23:19: And they shall prepare one male goat from the goats for a sin offering, and two year-old lambs for a sacrifice of deliverance, with the loaves of the firstfruits;
verses.23:20: and the priest shall present them with the loaves of the firstfruits as a presentation offering before the Lord, with the two lambs; they shall be holy to the Lord; to the priest who offers them, it shall belong to him.
verses.23:21: And you shall proclaim this day a convocation; it shall be holy to you; you shall do no servile work on it; it is an everlasting statute throughout your generations in all your dwelling.
verses.23:22: And when you reap the harvest of your land, you shall not finish reaping the remainder of the harvest of your field when you reap, nor shall you gather what falls from your harvest; for the poor and for the sojourner you shall leave it. I am the Lord your God.'"
verses.23:23: And the Lord spoke to Moses, saying,
verses.23:24: "Speak to the sons of Israel, saying: 'In the seventh month, on the first day of the month, there shall be a rest for you, a memorial of trumpets; it shall be a holy convocation to you.
verses.23:25: You shall do no servile work, and you shall bring a burnt offering to the Lord.'"
verses.23:26: And the Lord spoke to Moses, saying,
verses.23:27: "Also on the tenth day of this seventh month is the Day of Atonement; it shall be a holy convocation to you, and you shall humble your souls and bring a burnt offering to the Lord.
verses.23:28: You shall do no work on this very day, for it is a day of atonement for you, to make atonement for you before the Lord your God.
verses.23:29: Every soul that is not humbled on this very day shall be utterly destroyed from its people.
verses.23:30: And every soul that does any work on this very day, that soul shall perish from its people.
verses.23:31: You shall do no work; it is an everlasting statute throughout your generations in all your dwellings.
verses.23:32: It shall be a Sabbath of Sabbaths to you, and you shall humble your souls; from the ninth day of the month, from evening to evening, you shall keep your Sabbath."
verses.23:33: And the Lord spoke to Moses, saying,
verses.23:34: "Speak to the sons of Israel, saying: 'On the fifteenth day of this seventh month is the Feast of Tabernacles for seven days to the Lord.
verses.23:35: And the first day is a holy convocation; you shall do no servile work.
verses.23:36: For seven days you shall bring burnt offerings to the Lord; and the eighth day shall be a holy convocation to you, and you shall bring burnt offerings to the Lord; it is a closing festival; you shall do no servile work.
verses.23:37: These are the feasts to the Lord which you shall proclaim as holy convocations, to bring altar offerings to the Lord: burnt offerings and their sacrifices and their drink offerings, each day's portion on its day,
verses.23:38: besides the Sabbaths of the Lord, and besides your gifts, and besides all your vows, and besides your freewill offerings which you give to the Lord.
verses.23:39: And on the fifteenth day of this seventh month, when you have finished gathering the produce of the land, celebrate a feast to the Lord for seven days; on the first day there shall be rest, and on the eighth day there shall be rest.
verses.23:40: And you shall take on the first day choice fruit of a tree, and fronds of palm trees, and thick branches of a tree, and branches of willow and chaste-tree from a brook, to rejoice before the Lord your God seven days of the year;
verses.23:41: it is an everlasting statute throughout your generations. In the seventh month you shall celebrate it;
verses.23:42: in booths you shall dwell seven days; every native-born in Israel shall dwell in booths,
verses.23:43: so that your generations may see that I caused the sons of Israel to dwell in booths when I brought them out of the land of Egypt. I am the Lord your God.'"
verses.23:44: And Moses declared the feasts of the Lord to the sons of Israel.
verses.24:1: And the Lord spoke to Moses, saying,
verses.24:2: "Command the sons of Israel, and let them take for Me pure beaten olive oil for the light, to keep a lamp burning continually
verses.24:3: outside the veil in the tabernacle of testimony; Aaron and his sons shall keep it burning from evening until morning before the Lord continually; it is an everlasting statute throughout your generations.
verses.24:4: Upon the pure lampstand you shall keep the lamps burning before the Lord until morning.
verses.24:5: And you shall take fine flour and make it into twelve loaves; each loaf shall be of two tenths.
verses.24:6: And you shall place them in two rows, six loaves in one row, upon the pure table before the Lord.
verses.24:7: And you shall put upon the row pure frankincense and salt, and they shall be for loaves as a memorial, set forth to the Lord.
verses.24:8: On the Sabbath day it shall be set forth before the Lord continually, before the sons of Israel as an everlasting covenant.
verses.24:9: And it shall belong to Aaron and to his sons, and they shall eat them in a holy place; for this is most holy to them from the things sacrificed to the Lord, an everlasting statute."
verses.24:10: And the son of an Israelite woman went out, and he was the son of an Egyptian among the sons of Israel. And the son of the Israelite woman and the Israelite man fought in the camp,
verses.24:11: and the son of the Israelite woman, having named the Name, cursed. And they brought them to Moses; and his mother's name was Shelomith, the daughter of Dibri, of the tribe of Dan.
verses.24:12: And they put him in custody, to judge him by the command of the Lord.
verses.24:13: And the Lord spoke to Moses, saying,
verses.24:14: "Bring out the one who cursed outside the camp, and all who heard shall lay their hands upon his head, and all the congregation shall stone him.
verses.24:15: And speak to the sons of Israel, and you shall say to them: 'Any man who curses God shall bear sin,
verses.24:16: and whoever names the name of the Lord shall surely be put to death; all the congregation of Israel shall stone him with stones; whether sojourner or native-born, when he names the name of the Lord, let him die.
verses.24:17: And any man who strikes the life of a man, and he dies, shall surely be put to death.
verses.24:18: And whoever strikes an animal, and it dies, shall make restitution, life for life.
verses.24:19: And if anyone inflicts a blemish on his neighbor, as he has done to him, so shall it be done to him in return:
verses.24:20: fracture for fracture, eye for eye, tooth for tooth; just as he has inflicted a blemish on the man, so shall it be inflicted on him.
verses.24:21: Whoever strikes a man, and he dies, shall surely be put to death.
verses.24:22: There shall be one judgment for the sojourner and for the native of the land, for I am the Lord your God.'"
verses.24:23: And Moses spoke to the sons of Israel, and they brought the one who cursed outside the camp and stoned him with stones; and the sons of Israel did just as the Lord commanded Moses.
verses.25:1: And the Lord spoke to Moses on Mount Sinai, saying,
verses.25:2: "Speak to the sons of Israel, and you shall say to them: 'When you enter into the land which I give to you, then the land which I give to you shall rest a Sabbath to the Lord.
verses.25:3: Six years you shall sow your field, and six years you shall prune your vineyard and gather its fruit;
verses.25:4: but in the seventh year there shall be a Sabbath of rest for the land, a Sabbath to the Lord; you shall not sow your field, and you shall not prune your vineyard,
verses.25:5: and what springs up of itself in your field you shall not reap, and the grapes of your sanctification you shall not gather; it shall be a year of rest for the land.
verses.25:6: And the Sabbath of the land shall be food for you, and for your manservant, and for your maidservant, and for your hired worker, and for the sojourner who abides with you;
verses.25:7: and for your livestock and for the wild beasts that are in your land, all its produce shall be for food.
verses.25:8: And you shall count for yourself seven rests of years, seven years seven times; and seven weeks of years shall be to you forty-nine years.
verses.25:9: And you shall make proclamation with the sound of a trumpet throughout all your land, in the seventh month, on the tenth of the month; on the Day of Atonement you shall make proclamation with a trumpet throughout all your land.
verses.25:10: And sanctify the fiftieth year, and you shall proclaim release upon the land to all who dwell in it; this shall be to you a year, a signal of release, and each one shall depart to his possession, and each of you shall depart to his homeland.
verses.25:11: This is a signal of release; the fiftieth year shall be a year to you; you shall not sow, nor reap what springs up of itself in it, and you shall not gather its consecrated fruit;
verses.25:12: for it is a signal of release; it shall be holy to you; from the fields you shall eat its produce.
verses.25:13: In the year of release, at its signal, he shall return to his possession.
verses.25:14: And if you make a sale to your neighbor, or if you also buy from your neighbor, let no man oppress his neighbor.
verses.25:15: According to the number of years after the signal you shall buy from the neighbor; according to the number of years of produce he shall sell to you.
verses.25:16: According as the greater number of years increases his purchase, and according as the lesser number of years diminishes his possession—for the number of his produce he shall thus sell to you.
verses.25:17: Let no man oppress his neighbor, and you shall fear the Lord your God; I am the Lord your God.
verses.25:18: And you shall do all My ordinances and all My judgments, and keep them and do them, and you shall dwell in confidence;
verses.25:19: and the land shall yield its produce, and you shall eat to fullness, and you shall dwell upon it in confidence.
verses.25:20: And if you say, "What shall we eat in this seventh year, if we do not sow nor gather in our produce?"
verses.25:21: then I will send My blessing to you in the sixth year, and it shall bring forth its produce for the three years.
verses.25:22: And you shall sow in the eighth year, and you shall eat what is old from the produce; until the ninth year, until its produce comes in, you shall eat old of the old.
verses.25:23: And the land shall not be sold in perpetuity, for the land is Mine; because you are strangers and sojourners before Me;
verses.25:24: and throughout all the land of your possession you shall grant redemption for the land.
verses.25:25: And if your brother who is with you becomes poor and sells some of his possession, then his kinsman who is nearest to him shall come and shall redeem what his brother sold.
verses.25:26: And if anyone has no kinsman-redeemer, yet he prospers by his hand and enough is found for him for his redemption,
verses.25:27: then he shall calculate the years of his sale, and restore what he has to the man to whom he sold himself, and he shall depart to his possession.
verses.25:28: But if his hand is not found to have enough to restore them, then the sale shall remain with the one who bought them until the sixth year of the release; and it shall go out in the release, and he shall depart into his rest.
verses.25:29: And if anyone sells a dwelling house in a walled city, then there shall be redemption for it; until a year of days is completed, there shall be redemption for it.
verses.25:30: But if it is not redeemed until a whole year is completed for it, then the house that is in the city having a wall shall be confirmed permanently to the one who bought it, throughout his generations, and it shall not go out in the release.
verses.25:31: But the houses that are in villages, which have no wall around them, let them be reckoned as the field of the land; they shall be redeemable at all times, and in the release they shall go out.
verses.25:32: And as for the cities of the Levites, the houses of the cities of their possession shall be redeemable at all times for the Levites;
verses.25:33: and whoever redeems from the Levites, then their sale of the houses of the city of their possession shall go out in the release, because the houses of the cities of the Levites are their possession in the midst of the sons of Israel.
verses.25:34: And the fields set apart for their cities shall not be sold, because this is their everlasting possession.
verses.25:35: And if your brother becomes poor and grows weak in his hands beside you, you shall uphold him as a stranger and a sojourner, and your brother shall live with you.
verses.25:36: You shall not take from him interest nor with increase, and you shall fear your God; I am the Lord; and your brother shall live with you.
verses.25:37: You shall not give him your silver at interest, and you shall not give him your food for increase.
verses.25:38: I am the Lord your God, who brought you out of the land of Egypt to give you the land of Canaan, so as to be your God.
verses.25:39: And if your brother is brought low beside you and is sold to you, he shall not serve you with the service of a household servant;
verses.25:40: as a hired worker or a sojourner he shall be with you; until the year of release he shall work beside you,
verses.25:41: and he shall go out in the release, and his children with him, and he shall depart to his family; to his ancestral possession he shall hasten back.
verses.25:42: Because these are My household servants, whom I brought out of the land of Egypt, he shall not be sold in the sale of a household servant.
verses.25:43: You shall not wear him down with toil, and you shall fear the Lord your God.
verses.25:44: And as for manservant and maidservant, as many as you may have from the nations that are all around you, from them you shall acquire a male slave and a female slave.
verses.25:45: And from the sons of the sojourners who are among you, from these you shall acquire, and from their kindred, as many as are born in your land; let them be to you for a possession.
verses.25:46: And you shall apportion them to your children after you, and they shall be held as your possession forever; as for your brethren, the sons of Israel, each one shall not wear down his brother with toils.
verses.25:47: And if the hand of the stranger or of the sojourner beside you finds means, and your brother, being destitute, is sold to the stranger or to the sojourner beside you, to a stranger from birth,
verses.25:48: after he has been sold to him, there shall be redemption for him; one of your brothers shall redeem him.
verses.25:49: His father's brother or a son of his father's brother shall redeem him, or one from the kindred of his flesh from his tribe shall redeem him; or if, prospering by his hands, he redeems himself,
verses.25:50: then he shall reckon with the one who bought him from the year in which he sold himself to him until the year of release; and the silver of his sale shall be as that of a hired worker; year by year he shall be with him.
verses.25:51: And if more of the years remain for anyone, in proportion to these he shall repay his redemption from the silver of his sale;
verses.25:52: and if only a little remains of the years until the year of release, then he shall reckon with him according to his years, and he shall repay his redemption. As a hired worker,
verses.25:53: year by year he shall be with him; you shall not wear him down with toil in your sight.
verses.25:54: And if he is not redeemed after these things, he shall go out in the year of release, he and his children with him.
verses.25:55: For to Me the sons of Israel are household servants; these are My servants, whom I brought out of the land of Egypt.'"
verses.26:1: I am the Lord your God. You shall not make for yourselves handmade idols nor carved images, nor shall you set up a pillar for yourselves, nor shall you place a stone to gaze upon in your land to bow down to it; I am the Lord your God.
verses.26:2: You shall keep My Sabbaths and revere My sanctuaries; I am the Lord.
verses.26:3: If you walk in My ordinances, and keep My commandments and perform them,
verses.26:4: then I will give you the rain in its season, and the land shall yield its produce, and the trees of the fields shall yield their fruit.
verses.26:5: And for you the harvest shall overtake the vintage, and the vintage shall overtake the sowing; you shall eat your bread to the full, and dwell in security upon your land, and war shall not pass through your land.
verses.26:6: And I will give peace in your land, and you shall lie down, and there shall be no one to terrify you; and I will destroy evil beasts out of your land.
verses.26:7: And you shall pursue your enemies, and they shall fall before you by slaughter.
verses.26:8: And five of you shall pursue one hundred, and one hundred of you shall pursue tens of thousands, and your enemies shall fall before you by the sword.
verses.26:9: And I will look upon you, and I will cause you to increase and multiply you, and I will establish My covenant with you.
verses.26:10: And you shall eat old store, and the oldest of the old, and you shall bring out the old before the new.
verses.26:11: And I will set My covenant among you, and My soul shall not abhor you.
verses.26:12: And I will walk among you and be God to you, and you shall be My people.
verses.26:13: I am the Lord your God, who brought you out of the land of Egypt when you were slaves; and I shattered the bond of your yoke and led you forth with boldness.
verses.26:14: But if you do not obey Me, nor perform these ordinances of Mine,
verses.26:15: but disobey them, and your soul loathes My judgments, so that you do not perform all My commandments, so as to break My covenant,
verses.26:16: then I also will do thus to you: I will bring upon you perplexity, and the scab and jaundice, with your eyes wasting away and your soul melting away; and you shall sow your seeds in vain, and your adversaries shall eat them.
verses.26:17: And I will set My face against you, and you shall fall before enemies; and those who hate you shall pursue you, and you shall flee when no one pursues you.
verses.26:18: And if even up to this point you do not obey Me, then I will chastise you yet sevenfold for your sins.
verses.26:19: And I will shatter the arrogance of your pride, and I will make the sky iron for you and your earth like bronze.
verses.26:20: And your strength shall be in vain, and your land shall not yield its seed, and the tree of your field shall not yield its fruit.
verses.26:21: And if after these things you walk contrary and are not willing to obey Me, I will add to you seven plagues according to your sins.
verses.26:22: And I will send upon you the wild beasts of the earth, and they shall devour you and consume your livestock; and I will make you few in number, and your roads shall be made desolate.
verses.26:23: And if by these things you are not disciplined, but walk contrary to Me,
verses.26:24: then I also will walk with you in contrary wrath, and I also will strike you sevenfold for your sins.
verses.26:25: And I will bring upon you a sword avenging the justice of the covenant, and you shall flee for refuge into your cities; and I will send forth death among you, and you shall be delivered into the hands of enemies.
verses.26:26: When I afflict you with a scarcity of bread, ten women shall bake your loaves in one oven, and they shall return your loaves by weight; and you shall eat, and shall not be satisfied.
verses.26:27: But if in spite of these things you do not obey Me, and walk contrary to Me,
verses.26:28: then I Myself will walk with you in contrary wrath, and I will chastise you sevenfold according to your sins.
verses.26:29: And you shall eat the flesh of your sons, and the flesh of your daughters you shall eat.
verses.26:30: And I will lay waste your pillars, and I will utterly destroy your wooden handmade idols, and I will place your carcasses upon the carcasses of your idols; and My soul shall loathe you.
verses.26:31: And I will make your cities desolate, and I will lay waste your sanctuaries, and I will by no means smell the aroma of your sacrifices.
verses.26:32: And I Myself will lay waste your land, and your enemies who dwell in it shall be astonished at it.
verses.26:33: And I will scatter you among the nations, and the advancing sword shall consume you; and your land shall be desolate, and your cities shall be desolate.
verses.26:34: Then the land shall enjoy its Sabbaths, even all the days of its desolation,
verses.26:35: and you shall be in the land of your enemies; then the land shall keep Sabbath, and the land shall enjoy its Sabbaths. All the days of its desolation it shall keep the Sabbath rest which it did not keep during your Sabbaths, when you dwelt in it.
verses.26:36: And upon those who are left of you I will bring bondage into their heart in the land of their enemies; and the sound of a driven leaf shall pursue them, and they shall flee as those fleeing from war, and they shall fall when no one pursues.
verses.26:37: And brother shall disregard brother as in war when no one pursues, and you shall not be able to withstand your enemies.
verses.26:38: And you shall perish among the nations, and the land of your enemies shall devour you.
verses.26:39: And those who are left of you shall decay because of your sins; in the land of their enemies they shall pine away.
verses.26:40: And they shall confess their sins and the sins of their fathers, that they transgressed and disregarded Me, and that they walked contrary against Me,
verses.26:41: and I walked with them in contrary wrath; and I will destroy them in the land of their enemies. Then their uncircumcised heart shall be ashamed, and then they shall accept their sins.
verses.26:42: And I will remember the covenant of Jacob, and the covenant of Isaac and the covenant of Abraham I will remember; and the land I will remember.
verses.26:43: And the land shall be forsaken by them; then the land shall accept its Sabbaths when it is made desolate because of them, and they themselves shall accept their iniquities, because they disregarded My judgments and loathed My ordinances in their soul.
verses.26:44: And yet even so, while they are in the land of their enemies, I did not disregard them, nor did I loathe them so as to consume them utterly, to break My covenant with them; for I am the Lord their God.
verses.26:45: And I will remember for them the former covenant, when I brought them out of the land of Egypt, out of the house of bondage, in the sight of the nations, to be their God; I am the Lord.
verses.26:46: These are My judgments and My ordinances, and the law which the Lord gave between Himself and the sons of Israel on Mount Sinai by the hand of Moses.
verses.27:1: And the Lord spoke to Moses, saying,
verses.27:2: "Speak to the sons of Israel, and you shall say to them, 'Whoever vows a vow as a valuation of his soul to the Lord,
verses.27:3: the valuation of the male from twenty years old to sixty years old shall be—his valuation shall be fifty didrachmas of silver by the holy weight.
verses.27:4: And for the female, the assessed valuation shall be thirty didrachmas.
verses.27:5: And if from five years old to twenty years, the valuation of the male shall be twenty didrachmas, and of the female fourteen didrachmas.
verses.27:6: And from one month old to five years old, the valuation of the male shall be five didrachmas of silver, and of the female three didrachmas.
verses.27:7: And if from sixty years old and above, if it is a male, the valuation shall be fifteen didrachmas of silver; and if a female, ten didrachmas.
verses.27:8: But if he is too poor for the valuation, he shall stand before the priest, and the priest shall value him; just as the hand of him who vowed is able, the priest shall value him.
verses.27:9: Now if it is of the beasts from which a gift is offered to the Lord, whoever gives from these to the Lord, it shall be holy.
verses.27:10: He shall not exchange it, a good one for a bad one, nor a bad one for a good one; and if he does indeed exchange it, beast for beast, both it and the exchange shall be holy.
verses.27:11: And if it is any unclean beast, of those from which a gift is not offered to the Lord, he shall set the beast before the priest;
verses.27:12: and the priest shall value it between good and bad; and just as the priest values it, so shall it stand.
verses.27:13: But if he indeed redeems it, he shall add the fifth part to its valuation.
verses.27:14: And whatever man consecrates his house to be holy to the Lord, then the priest shall value it between good and bad; as the priest values it, so shall it stand.
verses.27:15: But if he who consecrated it redeems his house, he shall add to it the fifth part of the silver of the valuation, and it shall be his.
verses.27:16: And if a man consecrates to the Lord part of the field of his possession, then the valuation shall be according to its seed: for a kor of barley, fifty didrachmas of silver.
verses.27:17: And if he consecrates his field from the year of release, according to its valuation it shall stand.
verses.27:18: But if he consecrates his field later, after the release, the priest shall reckon to him the silver according to the remaining years until the year of release, and it shall be deducted from its assessed valuation.
verses.27:19: And if he who bought it redeems the field, he shall add the fifth part of the silver to its valuation, and it shall be his.
verses.27:20: But if he does not redeem the field, and sells the field to another man, he shall no longer redeem it;
verses.27:21: rather, the field, when the release goes out, shall be holy to the Lord, like the land that is set apart; it shall be a possession for the priest.
verses.27:22: And if he consecrates to the Lord part of a field which he has acquired, which is not of the field of his possession,
verses.27:23: the priest shall reckon to him the full amount of the valuation from the year of release, and he shall pay the valuation on that day as a holy thing to the Lord;
verses.27:24: and in the year of release the field shall be restored to the man from whom he acquired it, to whom the possession of the land belonged.
verses.27:25: And every valuation shall be by holy weights; twenty obols shall be the didrachma.
verses.27:26: And every firstborn that is born among your beasts shall belong to the Lord, and no one shall consecrate it, whether calf or sheep; it belongs to the Lord.
verses.27:27: But if it is of the unclean four-footed beasts, he shall exchange it according to its valuation and shall add the fifth part to it, and it shall be his; but if it is not redeemed, it shall be sold according to its valuation.
verses.27:28: Yet every devoted thing that a man devotes to the Lord from all that belongs to him, from man to beast, and from the field of his possession, shall not be sold nor redeemed; every devoted thing shall be most holy to the Lord.
verses.27:29: And whatever is devoted from among men shall not be redeemed, but shall surely be put to death.
verses.27:30: Every tithe of the land, of the seed of the land and of the fruit of the trees, belongs to the Lord; it is holy to the Lord.
verses.27:31: And if a man redeems his tithe by ransom, he shall add the fifth part to it, and it shall be his.
verses.27:32: And every tithe of oxen and of sheep, even everything that passes in the counting under the rod, the tenth shall be holy to the Lord.
verses.27:33: You shall not exchange a good one for a bad one; and if you do indeed exchange it, then its exchange also shall be holy; it shall not be redeemed.'"
verses.27:34: These are the commandments which the Lord commanded Moses for the sons of Israel on Mount Sinai.

notes.1:1: The Septuagint consistently renders the Hebrew 'tent of meeting' as 'tent of testimony' (skene tou martyriou), associating the meeting place with the testimony of the covenant.
notes.1:3: Greek dekton auto ('acceptable for him', also in 1:4) emphasizes the offering's acceptance before the Lord rather than the offerer's voluntary will as in the Hebrew Masoretic Text.
notes.1:4: Greek karpoma ('offering') designates an offering consumed by fire on the altar, distinct here from holokautoma ('whole burnt offering') and doron ('gift').
notes.1:11: The Greek preserves the explicit instruction 'and he shall lay his hand upon its head,' which is absent from the Hebrew Masoretic Text.
notes.2:1: Throughout chapter 2, the Septuagint uses thysia ('sacrifice') for the grain offering and adds the closing declaration 'It is a sacrifice' here.
notes.2:4: The Greek text reads ek libanou ('from frankincense'), a well-known Septuagint reading resulting from the omission of the initial letter of klibanou ('oven').
notes.2:14: Greek chidra ('groats') refers to fresh grains of unripe wheat that have been roasted and crushed.
notes.3:1: Greek thysia soteriou ('sacrifice of deliverance') is the Septuagint's characteristic rendering of the Hebrew peace or well-being offering.
notes.3:2: The Greek specifies plural 'hands' (also in 3:8 and 3:13) and uniquely names 'the altar of whole burnt offerings' in this verse.
notes.3:9: The Greek reads 'to God' rather than 'to the Lord' and renders the fat tail of the sheep as 'the unblemished loin' removed along with 'the flanks' (psoai, the loin muscles).
notes.3:11: Here and in 3:16 the Greek reads 'an aroma of sweet fragrance' where the Hebrew Masoretic Text reads 'food' or 'bread.'
notes.4:3: The Septuagint reads "the anointed high priest" and "causing the people to sin," whereas the Hebrew Masoretic Text reads "the anointed priest" and "bringing guilt on the people."
notes.4:5: The Septuagint adds "whose hands have been consecrated" (literally "perfected as to his hands"), a traditional Greek idiom for priestly ordination not present in the Hebrew Masoretic Text.
notes.4:10: The Septuagint reads the second-person plural "just as you take it away" and renders the Hebrew peace offering throughout Leviticus as "sacrifice of deliverance."
notes.4:12: Here and in verses 21, 24, 29, and 33, the Septuagint uses third-person plural verbs ("they shall carry," "they shall burn," "they shall slay") where the Hebrew Masoretic Text uses the singular.
notes.5:2: The Septuagint expands the list of sources of uncleanness to include an unclean animal torn by wild beasts and carcasses of unclean beasts, while omitting the Masoretic clause stating that the matter was hidden from him.
notes.5:4: The Septuagint uniquely reads "the lawless soul" where the Hebrew Masoretic Text reads "if a soul swears."
notes.5:15: Where the Hebrew Masoretic Text reads "commits a trespass," the Septuagint reads "genuinely forgets" (literally "it escapes him with forgetfulness"), reflecting a different reading of the underlying Hebrew root.
notes.5:20: In the Septuagint, Leviticus 5:20-26 continues chapter 5; in the Hebrew Masoretic Text and most English translations, these verses begin chapter 6 (Leviticus 6:1-7).
notes.5:24: The Septuagint reads "on the day he is convicted," whereas the Hebrew Masoretic Text reads "on the day of his guilt offering."
notes.6:3: Greek katakarposis literally denotes the burnt-up offering or consumed remains, corresponding to the Hebrew term for fatty ashes.
notes.6:7: Throughout Septuagint Leviticus, standalone thysia ("sacrifice") is used specifically for the grain or tribute offering.
notes.6:14: Greek helikta ("rolled pieces") refers to pastry or dough pieces rolled or twisted before being broken.
notes.6:15: Greek epitelesthesetai ("shall be completely offered") emphasizes the full completion of the rite, whereas the Hebrew reads "shall be wholly burned."
notes.7:1: The Septuagint explicitly specifies "of the ram" here and in verse two, identifying the animal required for the trespass offering.
notes.7:11: Greek soterion literally means "deliverance" or "salvation," serving as the Septuagint term for the peace or fellowship offering.
notes.7:15: The Septuagint includes "shall belong to him," assigning the flesh of the sacrifice of praise to the officiating priest.
notes.7:30: The Septuagint adds "and the lobe of the liver" alongside the fat on the breast, and uses "place a gift" (epitheinai doma) for the presentation rite.
notes.8:7: The Greek uses plural pronouns ("them") for the tunic and sash before shifting to the singular ("him") for Aaron's robe and ephod, differing from the singular pronouns throughout in the Hebrew text.
notes.8:8: The Septuagint renders the breastpiece as "the oracle" (logion) and translates the Urim and Thummim as "the Manifestation and the Truth" (delosis and aletheia).
notes.8:11: In the Septuagint, the anointing of the tabernacle and all its contents appears at the end of verse 11 rather than in verse 10 as in the Hebrew Masoretic Text.
notes.8:18: In this Greek text, the clauses corresponding to verse 19 in standard versification are joined directly to the end of verse 18.
notes.8:30: The Greek source repeats the sprinkling clause from the end of verse 29 and duplicates the final phrase "and the garments of his sons with him," reflecting textual overlap in the source witness.
notes.9:4: The Septuagint renders the Hebrew peace offering (shelamim) as "a sacrifice of deliverance" (thysia soteriou), emphasizing deliverance and well-being before the Lord.
notes.9:7: The Greek reads "for yourself and for your household," whereas the Hebrew Masoretic Text reads "for yourself and for the people."
notes.9:17: The Greek noun thysian ("offering") here refers to the grain offering of fine flour mixed with oil prescribed in verse 4; the Greek also specifies "his hands" in the plural.
notes.9:24: The Greek verb exeste ("were astounded") describes the people's awe and amazement, whereas the Hebrew text describes them shouting aloud.
notes.10:3: The Greek reads "in all the congregation" (Hebrew "before all the people") and renders Aaron's reaction with katenychthe ("was pierced to the heart"), whereas the Hebrew has "kept silent."
notes.10:4: The Greek preserves the Septuagint name forms Misadai (Hebrew Mishael), Elisaphan (Hebrew Elzaphan), and Aziel (Hebrew Uzziel), and describes Misadai and Elisaphan in plural apposition as "sons of the brother of Aaron's father."
notes.10:6: The Greek verb apokidaroo specifically means to remove the priestly turban (kidaris) from the head, and the final clause uses a passive verb ("with which they were burned by the Lord") rather than the Hebrew active ("which the Lord has kindled").
notes.10:18: The Greek phrase kata prosopon eso ("directly inside") stands at the head of the second clause in the Septuagint punctuation, modifying where the priests were to eat the offering.
notes.11:5: In verses 5 and 6, the Septuagint reverses the order of the hare (dasypoda, v. 5) and the rock badger (choirogryllion, v. 6) compared to the Hebrew Masoretic Text.
notes.11:14: Verse 15 (listing the raven in the Hebrew text) is absent from this Septuagint text, and the Greek bird name glaux ("owl") occurs in both verse 16 and verse 19.
notes.11:22: The four Greek insect names—brouchos, attakes, akris, and ophiomaches (literally "serpent-fighter")—denote varieties of locusts and grasshoppers, rendered here as wingless locust, cricket, locust, and grasshopper.
notes.11:47: The Septuagint uses the participle zoogonounton ("that bring forth living young") where the Hebrew has the general term for living creatures.
notes.12:3: The Greek uses the active verb περιτεμεῖ ("she shall circumcise"), continuing the mother as subject, whereas the Hebrew Masoretic Text uses a passive verb ("shall be circumcised").
notes.12:4: The Greek text reads ἐν αἵματι ἀκαθάρτῳ αὐτῆς ("in her unclean blood"; likewise in v. 5), differing from the Hebrew Masoretic Text ("in the blood of purification"). It also reads ἀγγίου ("vessel"), whereas other Greek manuscripts read ἁγίου ("holy thing").
notes.12:6: The Septuagint consistently renders Hebrew "tent of meeting" as σκηνῆς τοῦ μαρτυρίου ("tabernacle of witness").
notes.12:7: The Greek uses the active verb καθαριεῖ αὐτήν ("he shall cleanse her"), making the priest the subject, whereas the Hebrew reads "she shall be clean" (matching the passive verb used in v. 8).
notes.13:2: The Greek phrase oule semasias telauges ("a bright scar of a mark") presents a single composite description rather than the three separate skin conditions listed in the Hebrew Masoretic Text.
notes.13:4: The Greek text reads the feminine possessive pronoun autes ("her/its") with "flesh" and "skin" before switching to masculine autou ("his hair"); "his" is used here for English coherence. The Septuagint also uniquely includes "and it is dim" and directs the priest to isolate "the plague."
notes.13:11: The Septuagint reads affirmatively "and isolate him," in contrast to the Hebrew Masoretic Text, which states that the priest shall not shut him up.
notes.13:15: In the Septuagint, "the sound flesh" (rendered with hygies, "sound/healthy," corresponding to the "living flesh" of v. 14) is the grammatical subject that defiles the person.
notes.13:27: The Septuagint concludes this verse with "it has broken out in the sore" (echoing v. 22) even within the regulations concerning a burn (vv. 24–28).
notes.13:31: The Greek text reads traumatos ("of the wound") in the first clause and thrausmatos ("of the scale") in the second, and specifies "yellowish hair" where the Hebrew Masoretic Text reads "black hair."
notes.13:45: The Septuagint directs the leper to put a covering "around his mouth" and uses the passive "and he shall be called unclean," rather than the Hebrew Masoretic Text's active cry "Unclean, unclean."
notes.13:55: The Septuagint concludes with "it is fixed fast in the garment, or in the warp, or in the woof," in place of the Hebrew Masoretic Text's reference to a depression on the back or front of the fabric.
notes.14:10: The Greek measure 'cotyla' (roughly half a pint) renders the Hebrew liquid measure 'log.' The Greek also specifies 'yearling' for both the two lambs and the sheep.
notes.14:19: The Greek text reads 'the unclean one who is being cleansed from his sin,' whereas the Masoretic Text reads 'the one being cleansed from his uncleanness.'
notes.14:37: The Greek source text mentions only 'greenish hollows,' without the additional 'or reddish' found in the Masoretic Text.
notes.14:39: Following Codex Vaticanus, the Greek source text reads 'has not spread,' in contrast to the Masoretic Text and other witnesses that read 'has spread.'
notes.14:42: The Greek text specifies 'solid scraped stones' where the Masoretic Text reads 'other stones.'
notes.15:3: Greek rheon gonon ("flowing with an issue/seed") introduces the discharge terminology used throughout the chapter (gonorrhues). The Septuagint reads sunesteken ("is stopped up") and includes an expanded final clause not present in the Hebrew Masoretic Text.
notes.15:9: The Septuagint specifies "of a donkey" (onou) and adds "until evening" (heos hesperas), both absent from the Hebrew Masoretic Text.
notes.15:23: The Septuagint reads a genitive absolute ("while she is on her bed") and feminine autes ("when he touches her"), followed by the neuter akatharton ("unclean"), translated "he shall be unclean" in agreement with the preceding masculine pronoun auton.
notes.15:31: Greek eulabeis poiesete ("make cautious" or "make reverent") reflects a distinctive Septuagint rendering of the Hebrew verb commonly translated "separate" or "warn."
notes.16:1: The Septuagint explicitly adds "strange fire" (pur allotrion, echoing Leviticus 10:1), where the Hebrew Masoretic Text reads "when they drew near before the Lord."
notes.16:8: Greek to apopompaio (lit. "for the one to be sent away," traditionally "for the scapegoat") renders the Hebrew term Azazel; see also "for dismissal" (eis ten apopompen) in 16:10 and "set apart for release" (ton diestalmenon eis aphesin) in 16:26.
notes.16:20: The Septuagint includes the additional clause "and he shall make cleansing for the priests" (compare also the Septuagint additions "and for his house" and "as for the priests" in 16:24).
notes.16:29: This Greek text reads "in the seventh month" without the words "on the tenth day of the month" found in the Hebrew Masoretic Text and some Greek witnesses.
notes.16:34: The Septuagint reads a future passive verb, "Once a year it shall be done" (poiethesetai), where the Hebrew Masoretic Text concludes with the active narrative statement "And he did as the Lord commanded Moses."
notes.17:3: The Greek explicitly includes proselytes (proselutos, resident foreigners who have joined Israel) and those attached among them, and specifies a calf (moschos) where the Hebrew reads an ox.
notes.17:4: The Septuagint contains a notable expansion specifying burnt offerings and offerings of deliverance (soterion, the Greek rendering for the peace offering) as well as a repeated clause on slaughtering outside the camp.
notes.17:7: Greek tois mataiois ("the vain things") is a standard Septuagint designation for worthless idols, standing where the Hebrew reads "goat-demons."
notes.17:11: The Greek states that the life of all flesh "is its blood" (rather than "is in the blood") and uses the substitutionary preposition anti ("in place of the soul") for the blood's atoning role.
notes.18:6: Throughout this chapter, the Septuagint renders the Hebrew idiom "nakedness" with the modest term aschemosyne (literally "indecency" or "shame").
notes.18:17: The Greek reads "your close relatives" (sou), whereas the Hebrew text reads "her near kinswomen."
notes.18:21: The Septuagint renders this prohibition as giving offspring "to serve a ruler" (latreuein archonti) and profaning "the holy name," where the Hebrew refers to passing children through the fire to Molech and profaning "the name of your God."
notes.18:25: Here and in verse 28, the Septuagint renders the vivid Hebrew metaphor of the land "vomiting out" its inhabitants with prosochthizo ("to loathe" or "be disgusted with").
notes.19:3: The Septuagint places 'his father' before 'his mother,' reversing the order found in the Hebrew Masoretic Text.
notes.19:5: The Greek reads 'a sacrifice of deliverance' (thysian soterioy) and 'your tenth' (dekaten hymon, i.e., tithe), whereas some other Greek witnesses read 'acceptable for you' (dekten hymin), closer to the Hebrew.
notes.19:26: The Septuagint reads 'upon the mountains' (epi ton oreon), diverging from the Hebrew Masoretic Text's prohibition against eating 'with the blood.'
notes.19:36: The Greek specifies a 'chous' (chous), a standard Greek liquid measure of roughly three liters, where the Hebrew lists an ephah and a hin.
notes.20:2: Here and in 20:3-5, the Septuagint renders the Hebrew name Molech as 'ruler' (archonti; plural 'rulers' in 20:5).
notes.20:3: The Greek reads 'the name of those sanctified to Me' (to onoma ton hegiasmenon moi), whereas the Hebrew text has 'My holy name.'
notes.20:9: Here and in 20:11-13, 16, and 27, the Septuagint renders the Hebrew idiom 'his/their blood shall be upon him/them' as 'he shall be guilty' or 'they are guilty' (enochos).
notes.20:20: The Septuagint uses the broader term 'his kinswoman' (tes syngenous autou) where the Hebrew specifies 'his uncle's wife.'
notes.21:4: Greek exapina ("suddenly") is a distinctive Septuagint rendering where the Masoretic Text has a difficult Hebrew phrase often understood as "as a leader" or "as a husband."
notes.21:8: Greek hagiasei auton ("he shall sanctify him") is third-person singular rather than the second-person singular of the Masoretic Text; it may also be understood reflexively ("sanctify himself") or with the Lord as subject.
notes.21:10: Greek apokidarosei specifically refers to removing the priestly turban (kidaris) from the head, interpreting the Hebrew command not to leave the head uncovered or disheveled.
notes.21:20: The Greek medical terms ephelos ("having white spots in the eye"), ptilos ("blear-eyed"), and monorchis ("having only one testicle") represent specific Septuagint interpretations of rare Hebrew blemish terms.
notes.22:9: The Greek text places the conditional clause "and if they profane them" before the closing divine formula and includes the title "God" in "the Lord God who sanctifies them."
notes.22:13: The Greek text reads chera ekbeblemene ("a widow, one cast out") without a conjunction ("or") between the two descriptors.
notes.22:23: Greek sphagia poieseis auta seauto ("you may make them as slaughter-offerings for yourself") permits domestic slaughter rather than a freewill offering as in the Masoretic Text, and kolobokerkon specifies an animal docked in the tail.
notes.22:29: Greek thusian euchen charmosunes ("a sacrifice, a vow of gladness") emphasizes a joyful votive offering where the Masoretic Text reads "a sacrifice of thanksgiving."
notes.23:4: The Greek reads 'and these, proclaim them holy' as an imperative clause, differing from the Hebrew relative clause ('holy convocations, which you shall proclaim').
notes.23:11: The Greek specifies 'on the day after the first day' (referring to the first day of Unleavened Bread), reflecting an early interpretive tradition for the Hebrew phrase 'the day after the Sabbath.'
notes.23:36: The Greek term exodion ('closing festival' or 'day of departure') renders the Hebrew designation for the solemn concluding assembly at the end of the Feast of Tabernacles.
notes.23:40: The Greek lists branches of both willow and chaste-tree from a brook and attaches 'of the year' to the end of verse 40 rather than verse 41.
notes.24:7: The Greek adds 'and salt' alongside pure frankincense upon the loaves, harmonizing with the requirement of salt for offerings in Leviticus 2:13.
notes.24:11: The Greek describes the offense as 'having named the Name, cursed' and uses the plural 'brought them,' bringing both combatants before Moses.
notes.24:16: The Greek renders the prohibition as 'whoever names the name of the Lord,' a wording historically linked to the reverent Jewish custom of not pronouncing the divine Name aloud.
notes.24:21: The Greek contains only the clause concerning striking a human being, omitting the repetition of the animal-restitution rule already given in verse 18.
notes.25:5: The Greek 'grapes of your sanctification' reflects the Septuagint's rendering of the Hebrew term for untrimmed vines as something consecrated, akin to a Nazirite vow (cf. verse eleven).
notes.25:10: The phrase 'signal of release' is the Septuagint's rendering of the Jubilee, highlighting the trumpet-signal announcing liberty throughout the land (cf. verses eleven through thirteen and fifteen).
notes.25:27: The Septuagint reads 'what he has' and 'to whom he sold himself,' differing from the Hebrew Masoretic Text's 'the surplus' and 'to whom he sold it.'
notes.25:28: The Greek uniquely reads 'until the sixth year of the release' and 'into his rest,' whereas the Hebrew Masoretic Text has 'until the year of jubilee' and 'to his possession.'
notes.25:55: The Septuagint concludes the chapter with the Exodus reminder and omits the closing formula 'I am the Lord your God' found in the Hebrew Masoretic Text.
notes.26:1: The Greek text begins with the declaration 'I am the Lord your God' and renders the forbidden cultic stone as 'lithon skopon' (literally a lookout stone or stone set up to gaze upon), reflecting an interpretation of the Hebrew term as connected with looking or viewing.
notes.26:11: The Septuagint reads 'My covenant' (diatheken) here, whereas the Hebrew Masoretic Text reads 'My dwelling' or 'My tabernacle.'
notes.26:21: Here and in verses 23, 24, 27, 28, 40, and 41, the Greek uses 'plagios' (literally sideways, crooked, or contrary) both for Israel's willful opposition and for the Lord's responding wrath.
notes.26:36: The Greek critical text reads 'doulian' ('bondage/servitude'), whereas other Septuagint manuscripts read 'deilian' ('timidity/faintheartedness').
notes.26:41: The Septuagint reads the future 'I will destroy them' (apolo) rather than the Masoretic Text's 'I brought them,' and uses 'eudokesousin' ('accept' or 'acquiesce in,' i.e., the penalty of their sins), echoing the same verb used for the land enjoying its Sabbaths in verses 34-35.
notes.27:3: The Greek text renders the Hebrew sanctuary shekel as the didrachma (a two-drachma silver coin, valued at twenty obols in verse 25) and refers to the sanctuary standard as the holy weight.
notes.27:5: The Greek text reads fourteen didrachmas for a female aged five to twenty, whereas the Hebrew Masoretic Text reads ten shekels.
notes.27:19: The Greek text reads he who bought it, whereas the Hebrew Masoretic Text reads he who consecrated it.
notes.27:23: The Greek text uses release throughout this chapter for the Jubilee year and here reads from the year of release, whereas the Hebrew Masoretic Text reads until the year of Jubilee.
